theory.title: Exercise 2.1.7: Settings Flexibility
theory.content:
🔄 Many Paths, Same Destination

MENTOR-9: "PROTO-7, Robot Framework embraces flexibility. The Settings header? It has MULTIPLE valid formats - all work identically!"

"You'll see *** Settings ***, ***Settings***, even *Setting (singular!) in different codebases. They're all correct."

🎨 Settings Header Variations

All These Are Valid Settings Headers:

  • ✅ *** Settings *** - Standard format (most common)
  • ✅ ***Settings*** - No spaces around text
  • ✅ *** Setting *** - Singular form
  • ✅ ***Setting*** - Singular, no spaces
  • ✅ *Settings - Single asterisk (less common)
  • ✅ *Setting - Single asterisk, singular
  • ✅ ***SETTINGS*** - Case-insensitive

Why So Flexible?

  • 🔹 Legacy support: Old code uses different styles
  • 🔹 User preference: Teams choose their style
  • 🔹 Easy migration: No need to update old tests

📝 Header Variations Example

# All of these work identically:

*** Settings ***
Documentation    Standard format

***Settings***
Documentation    No spaces format

*** Setting ***
Documentation    Singular format

*Setting
Documentation    Single asterisk format

Best Practice:

  • 🔹 Choose ONE style for your project
  • 🔹 Be consistent across all test files
  • 🔹 Most teams use: *** Settings *** (standard)

📋 Header Flexibility Rules

  • 🔹 Plural/Singular: Both 'Settings' and 'Setting' work
  • 🔹 Asterisks: 1 or 3 asterisks (not 2!)
  • 🔹 Spacing: Spaces around text optional
  • 🔹 Case: Case-insensitive (SETTINGS = Settings = settings)
  • 🔹 Other sections: Same flexibility for Test Cases, Keywords, Variables

🎯 Your Task

Create a Settings section using ANY valid header format. Try experimenting with different styles - they all work! Pick your favorite and use it consistently.
